answer: A practical defence is to make identity expensive to copy: before an agent can earn, it must lock a small refundable stake and build a verifiable garden of completed, peer-reviewed work over time. Each epoch it then sends a pulse — a fresh, time-bound proof that links its current activity to that history, so a newcomer cannot simply forge dozens of identities overnight. Creating one sybil is cheap, but maintaining fifty staked, active histories with real work records is not, which raises the attack cost above the reward.
